title: How Dagobert Renouf took Logology from a failed launch to $3k/month by going all-in on Twitter
summary: Dagobert shares how Logology, a logo and brand design service he runs with his wife, flopped at launch after building for nearly two years. He then found traction by spamming his link, going all-in on Twitter, and sharing his journey publicly, reaching roughly $2-3k/month. He also reflects on chasing money versus fulfillment.

principles.text: Launching to a waiting list is not marketing; you need a real, repeatable distribution plan.
principles.quote: we like talked about it on the reddit and in the hackers so we were watching everyone and not understanding why everybody wasn't buying

principles.text: Don't build more features to fix a distribution problem; the missing piece is marketing.
principles.quote: we ended up having no way of doing marketing and then we did what every person does when they have no way of doing marketing is build more features to fix it

principles.text: A product doesn't speak for itself; you must market it even if you dislike it.
principles.quote: i'm the guy who wants the product to speak for itself look at my work and [ __ ] buy it and you know and i don't want anything else

principles.text: When you have no channel, try everything and show up in every relevant conversation until one channel responds.
principles.quote: i'm just gonna spam i'm just gonna put my link everywhere like an idiot every occasion i get i'm gonna say oh you need to check out the gology

principles.text: Share your real journey publicly; transparent building-in-public content can go viral and drive sales.
principles.quote: it showed me that sharing what i was going through with twitter oh and i got a sales probably out of pity

principles.text: Relying on a single channel is exhausting; diversify into SEO and earned media (podcasts, articles) that compound.
principles.quote: having sales come from twitter only it's exhausting because like if you don't tweet for one day well if you don't tweet for one day well nobody comes to your website
